editorial:
Imagine if one of history's most famous killers stole a time machine and landed right in the middle of San Francisco. That is exactly what happens here, and it sets up a wild chase that feels like a mix of a detective story and a sci-fi romp. You get to follow H.G. Wells, the actual author of The Time Machine, as he hunts down Jack the Ripper to stop him from killing again. The vibe is lighthearted but still has some tension, making it a great pick for a movie night when you want something clever but not too heavy.

What really makes this work is the chemistry between the characters and the fish-out-of-water humor as the villains try to understand the modern world. The pacing is snappy, and while the special effects are old, they still have a lot of charm. If you enjoy stories about time travel and mystery, you will love this. Since it is an older film, your best bet is to track down a 4K Blu-ray for your physical collection to get the best picture, or you can easily rent it on Apple TV for a quick watch.
endingExplained: In the final showdown, Wells manages to trick the Ripper into a trap. After a tense struggle, the Ripper is finally defeated and killed, ending his reign of terror once and for all. Wells then uses the time machine to return to his own time in the 19th century. He realizes that the future is a strange place, but he is happy to go home and write his famous books knowing the world is safe.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves time travel and historical mysteries.
